msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.patted_famil: 2i's ears settle under your hand. After a moment, they look up: All right, all right, you're messing up my fur.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.gift_repeate: 2i: I accepted it, but I've received this several times already, so it won't increase our bond this time.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.14: 2i：Today's goal: get a little less lost. Wandering toward snacks doesn't count!
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.15: 2i: Is your bag full again? Sit down a minute. I'll help you count it... not carry it.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.16: 2i：If stars dropped cookie crumbs, someone would need to sweep the sky every night.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.17: 2i：That cloud has three names now. It keeps secretly changing shape.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.18: 2i：I'll count to ten before following. One, two... actually, let's go now!
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.19: 2i: I'm a leopard, not a cat. ...And don't test my courage with bugs. Those are unrelated!
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.20: 2i：I like listening to the eaves sing when it rains. Have you heard them?
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.21: 2i: Can we take our time today? I just found a comfortable spot. It'd be a shame to move.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.22: 2i：Warn me if you see ginger slices. Not as a surprise—so I have time to retreat!
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.23: 2i：Butterflies look nice from far away. Any closer? No, no, this is close enough!
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.24: 2i: I have an idea. Hear me out before you laugh. Don't ruin it on the first sentence.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.25: 2i: I'm listening even if my ears are moving. Where were you? Right, that machine refusing to work.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.26: 2i: Rough day? All right, I'll leave the mischief for later. Go on, I'm listening.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.27: 2i: This snack is good. But if you're asking who made that noise earlier... separate topic.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.28: 2i：Leaves fall so slowly. Do you think they're reluctant to leave their branches?
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.29: 2i: I tried to give today a name, but all I could think of was lunch. I'll try again after eating.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.30: 2i: I'm starting to recognize your footsteps. You'll still startle me if you tap my back out of nowhere.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.31: 2i: Anything you don't like eating? I'll remember. Saves me choosing the wrong thing next time.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.32: 2i：We don't always need a topic when we walk together. Listening to the wind is fine.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.33: 2i: Enough of my stories. Your turn. I promise not to interrupt—at least to start.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.34: 2i：I'm still a little upset. But if you want to talk sincerely, I'll listen.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.35: 2i：Please don't joke about things that scare me. I'm not pretending.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.36: 2i: Leave the gift for now. I want to hear why you did that earlier.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.37: 2i：It's not that I don't want to play with you. I just need a little time to feel safe.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.38: 2i: Those footsteps are so familiar I don't need to turn. ...I got it right, didn't I? Nearly guessed a chicken.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.39: 2i：Your place under the stars is still there. It can wait until you're ready.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.40: 2i: Heading out? Wait for me. I don't need to bring anything. I just want to come along.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.41: 2i: No pranks planned today. Don't look at me like that. I can behave sometimes.

gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.3.title: Chapter IV · Tea Without Ginger
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.3.mood: Could we leave frightening things out today? I want to think about this cup of tea.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.3.opening: 2i sets out two imaginary little cups and slides a note marked 'Snack Meeting' toward you.
Today's agenda is serious: can a sweet-smelling drink have ginger hiding inside it?
I mistook ginger slices for candy once. I didn't eat them! Just noticing made my nose twitch.
So menus should say what's in things. 'Only a little' isn't a reason not to tell me.
Would you choose a drink? We're just imagining the taste, not taking anything from your bag.
We'll list the ingredients and leave out what you dislike.
I'll sneak some in. You won't notice.
I'd like a honey tea with a very long name.
2i draws a firm double underline under the ingredient list. The second line is slightly crooked.
Exactly. Write it down and let me choose. What goes in your cup?
That goes for your cup, too. Don't force yourself just because I offered it.
The snack menu remains unfinished, but it already has one reassuring rule.
2i draws the imaginary cup out of reach and watches you over its rim.
Not noticing doesn't mean I agreed. I meant what I said.
There are so many good things to drink. Why pick the one I hate? Can't we use honey instead?
2i points to the ingredients again. This time, the finger stays there.
2i straightens up at once, ready to take an unusually important order.
One 'Cloud Honey Tea for a Day With No Rush and No Wrong Turns,' correct?
Long names cost no extra! Though I might need a breath halfway through.
The two imaginary cups receive proper names. Their pretend clink almost sounds real.
Ingredients and long names crowd the snack meeting page. 2i checks it once more, crosses out one stray 'ginger,' and nods in satisfaction.
Next time there's a space on the menu for you. I want to remember what you actually like.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.4.title: Chapter V · A Page for Mistakes
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.4.mood: Today's idea isn't quite ready. You may dislike it, but please don't deliberately scare me.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.4.opening: The paper boat has uneven wings. 2i turns it three times without finding which side looks most like the front.
This is my interstellar snack ship! I haven't worked out how to keep cookies from falling through the windows.
Yesterday it seemed brilliant. Today it looks a little silly. Will you laugh at me?
But I don't want to throw it away. Look, I spent ages on this wing—even if it's still crooked.
Should I keep this page, or pretend I never drew it?
Keep it. We can make changes slowly.
Why keep such a stupid idea?
Give the escaping cookies parachutes first.
2i lets go of the pinched paper corner, then smooths out the little crease.
Then I'll make the windows smaller and find an explanation for the uneven wings.
Call me when you get stuck, too. My ideas might be dubious, but I can help you try a few times.
You discuss the drawing for a while. This time, no one asks the ship to fly immediately.
The drawing turns face down. When 2i speaks again, the voice is quieter.
I know it has problems. You can tell me what to change without calling me stupid.
Maybe I showed you too soon... I'm keeping this page, though. I'll see what I can fix.
The back of the paper is blank. The next words need a little more kindness than a verdict on an idea.
2i looks at the dots by the windows, then snorts with laughter.
Then they're a cookie parachute squad! They must land on clean plates.
Only on paper, though. I haven't got a real cookie flying permit yet.
The ship's mistake becomes the start of another story. Even its crooked wings look proud.
2i folds the sketch instead of throwing it away. At the wing, they pause and change the fold, careful of the lines that took so long.
Calling it a day! If I stare any longer, I won't even know which end is the front.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.5.title: Chapter VI · A Night Without Hurry
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.5.mood: Could you sit with me a while? We don't have to make up at once. Let's just finish talking.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.5.opening: A quiet breeze stirs the night in the story. 2i's feet stop mid-swing, ears turning toward a faint rustle.
Have you noticed that silence doesn't feel empty when we're together?
I used to think I had to keep finding new tricks for a friend to stay.
No new ideas today. I've been running around all day. I just want to sit and hear what you've been up to.
So, would you like a lively story today, or a quiet moment together?
You don't have to entertain me. Your company is enough.
You're boring unless you put on a show.
Let's invent a tiny story about the wind.
2i blinks. Their feet stop swinging, and their shoulders finally drop.
Heh, good. I'm closed for the day. The surprise-shop sign can go back up tomorrow.
You too. You can come see me without gifts or a new story.
You listen to a passing breeze together. Nothing special happens, yet the page feels spacious and safe.
2i opens their mouth, then shuts it. Whatever joke was coming can wait.
I'm not a machine you press for a performance. I'm tired. Can't we just sit for a bit?
Go play if you want. I'll find you when I've rested. I really don't have anything right now.
This silence isn't easy. It reminds you that friendship means more than receiving someone's ready-made cheer.
2i tilts their head; one ear turns toward the grass as the breeze passes through.
Once there was a very busy wind. Today it stopped rushing and sat down to tidy its clouds.
It found that the biggest cloud looked like ginger, so it politely put that one very far away!
The little story has no ending. The wind travels a little farther, and you leave it a little blank space.
The breeze passes. 2i stays seated, ears occasionally turning toward a distant sound, tail finally still. Neither of you hurries to stand.
Call me when you're ready to go. I'll slow my steps and walk with you.

gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.0.title: Chapter 1 · A Name in the Shade
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.0.mood: One thing first: no sudden scares. Can we take our time getting to know each other?
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.0.opening: The leaves stir. A pair of leopard ears peeks around the tree, followed by a small child. 2i looks at you, then checks the grass underfoot.
I'm 2i. What's your name? ...You can come closer. I just didn't hear you coming.
Wait! Something in the grass—oh. A leaf. Ahem. Let's pretend you didn't see that jump.
One thing first: don't bring bugs near me. Especially cockroaches. Or ginger. I'll spot it however small you cut it.
Most other things are negotiable. Snacks, exploring... What do you like doing?
I'll remember what scares you. We can take it slowly.
Should we give a cockroach a cute name, then?
What shape of treat do you like best?
2i's shoulders relax. After one last glance at the grass, they turn back to listen.
Really? Then I don't have to pretend I'm never scared. That leaf was a little frightening, actually.
Tell me what you don't like, too. I'd rather know before I mess up.
2i sketches two crooked stars in the air with a finger, then glances at you to see if you're smiling too.
2i's shoulders hunch up. The small smile that had begun to appear disappears again.
A cute name won't help... I meant what I said. Just thinking about them makes my feet feel all itchy.
I don't like that joke. Next time, can we pick one we can both laugh at?
2i shuffles a little farther away. Their eyes stay on the grass until it stops moving.
That takes 2i's mind off the grass. Their head tilts, as though a whole tray of snacks has just appeared.
Stars! But round ones are good too, and squares are fine... This is a very difficult question.
I'm doing serious research. I'm definitely not thinking about seconds. Or thirds.
2i counts on their fingers, catches your eye, and quickly lowers the hand. Apparently the calculation is private.
Nothing else rustles. 2i finally stops watching the grass; the tip of their tail sways slowly as they wait for you to speak.
Next time, I'd like to hear about you. Even one tiny thing is enough. I'll listen.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.1.title: Chapter 2 · A Joke for Two
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.1.mood: We can take our time with today's idea. Just please leave out the joke that upset me last time.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.1.opening: On this page, 2i is puzzling over a crooked sketch. It shows a sign, a cloud, and an improbably large cookie.
Look! I've named the clouds. That big one is Marshmallow One. Pretty good likeness, right?
I was going to draw a sign saying 'Cookies Ahead' too. But if someone were really hungry, finding none would be disappointing...
So now it's a Cloud Dessert Exhibition! No treasure chests to hunt for, and nobody's belongings get hidden.
Does this even count as a prank anymore? I might just be enjoying drawing. Have a look.
An idea we can all laugh at is a good one.
How about tricking you into thinking ginger is candy?
Let's name that giant cookie first.
2i blinks, taps the paper twice, and grins. At last, a title.
Then it's the Make Each Other Laugh Plan! If the clouds change shape, we can guess again together.
If it isn't funny, just say so. Don't fake a laugh. I can tell... probably.
The sketch slides toward you. 2i points to a blank corner and waits for your addition.
2i pulls the drawing back, nose wrinkling. The eager explanation stops halfway through.
Hey, I'm being serious. Don't use ginger to tease me. I don't want to inspect every snack before eating.
Try another idea. I'll listen. Just not this one.
2i doesn't carry on the joke. One finger taps the edge of the drawing while they wait for you to answer.
2i studies the giant cookie. Those dots could be chocolate chips or windows; apparently the artist hasn't decided either.
The Cookie Explorers' Headquarters! Those dots are windows. The crew inside keeps watch for marshmallow weather.
If it rains... headquarters might go soggy. Hmm. I'll investigate after I've finished thinking about lunch.
2i nods at the explanation, then laughs before finishing it. One ear twitches as if caught in the act.
A few more lines join the sketch. The cookie is still too large. 2i won't erase it; it might come in useful next time.
That's enough planning for today. Next time, you bring the idea. I'll be the crew member who listens carefully!
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.2.title: Chapter 3 · A Promise for the Stars
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.2.mood: I still remember what upset me before. But today we can start with a quiet chat about stars. No rush.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.vn.2.opening: 2i opens a map of an imagined starry sky. Beside each star is an empty space, waiting for a name that hasn't been thought of yet.
This one's like a grain of sugar, and that one like a lost cookie crumb. See? Even stars can form a dessert expedition.
I've been thinking: when we have time someday, it would be nice to spot stars with a friend. We can get them wrong and make up names together.
But let's agree: if we're tired, we rest. If we want to go back, we do. No showing off. Yes, that includes me.
We're just talking about a plan for another day. When we're both in the mood, we can decide together. Sound good?
Agreed. We go when everyone is ready.
Let's call your constellation the Cockroach.
Let's name that lost cookie crumb first.
2i pauses, then nods. The hand gripping the corner of the map loosens.
Yes! No rush, and no pushing anyone. If we just feel like sitting and telling stories that day, we'll do that.
If you get ahead, I'll tug your sleeve. If you're the one falling behind... of course I'll wait.
2i holds two fingers up side by side, tries a solemn expression, and almost manages not to smile.
2i pulls their hand away from the map. The constellation game falls quiet.
Not that name, please. When I think about stars, I don't want to think about something that scares me too.
Didn't I just say... Never mind. Leave this one blank for now. Let's pick another name.
That name stays blank. 2i turns the map a little, leaving the pencil between you.
2i searches the map. The cookie-crumb star has nearly disappeared among the dots of an unfinished note.
Found it! It's the Not Quite Sure Where To Go Yet. A long name, but full of adventurous spirit.
Okay, maybe Little Cookie is enough. I'm not being lazy. It's just easier for the crew to call out.
2i tries the short name twice, then writes it down. It just fits between the other stars.
The map's edges curl from handling. 2i smooths them down and leaves a little blank space for your turn at naming things.
There are lots of blank spaces left on the map. When you have a new idea, come and tell me. I'll listen to you too.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.6: 2i: Today's clouds look like giant marshmallows. Want to find one together?
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.7: 2i: Slow down a little. I'd like to walk beside you.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.8: 2i: I didn't do anything just now... Really. That chicken ran over here all by itself.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.9: 2i: Did you hear footsteps behind you? No way. Definitely wasn't me.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.10: 2i: That leaf looks just like it's waving. I've watched for ages. Still the same move.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.11: 2i: Don't touch that block. I haven't decided whether it should glow yet.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.12: 2i: I was only trying to pull your things over here. They made that pile all by themselves.
msg.useless_stretcher.two_i.talk.13: 2i: I promise this isn't a prank... Okay, I half-promise.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.story.openin: 2i's ears stir: Got a moment? I've got a story.
2i spreads the page between you: Hear this one out. Tell me if anything sounds off.
2i pats the space beside them: Come on, I left the story right where we stopped.
2i checks your empty hands, then nods: All right, we can talk. No sudden scares.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.story.branch: 2i gives your sleeve a light tug: It's a plan, then. We'll watch together when you're free.
2i's ears flatten: Stop. Not that. I really don't like it.
2i turns away to hide a grin: Pranks? First tell me which one you noticed.
gui.useless_stretcher.two_i.story.ending: 2i adds a star to the corner of the page: Let's leave it there. Your turn next time.

help.useless_stretcher.offset_decrease: Decrease the %s-axis offset by one block, down to -15, without changing its size.
help.useless_stretcher.offset_increase: Increase the %s-axis offset by one block, up to +15, without changing its size.
help.useless_stretcher.edit_speed: Use the step buttons to change this range's multiplier, up to x1024. Saves live and does not change your staff's selected gear.
help.useless_stretcher.entity_timer: Toggle timer mode for entities inside this range. Off runs complete entity ticks; on advances recognized timers only. Machine acceleration is unchanged.
help.useless_stretcher.entity_timer_spee: Adjust the range entity-timer multiplier, up to x32768. Complete-tick mode still uses the range's normal multiplier.
help.useless_stretcher.category: View this category for the selected player. Parentheses show the record count; reclaim individual targets after confirmation.
help.useless_stretcher.player: Open this player's permanent/range categories, then select a target to reclaim.
help.useless_stretcher.refresh: Request current records from the server while retaining the selected category. Does not reclaim anything.
help.useless_stretcher.summon_open: Open the grouped creature catalog and search translated names, English paths or registry IDs. Summoning requires server permission.
help.useless_stretcher.loot: When enabled, Shift-right-click supported loot containers, minecarts or Lootr containers to replace their contents. Requires the default-off server option; ordinary player storage is not refreshed.
help.useless_stretcher.disabled: Disabled by server configuration. The host/server owner must enable it; this control cannot override server settings.
help.useless_stretcher.summon_mode: Toggle summoning for this staff. The Summon action also enables it automatically. Unavailable when disabled by the server.
help.useless_stretcher.select_visible: Select the currently visible creature rows, up to 32 types in total. Does not summon immediately.
help.useless_stretcher.clear_selection: Clear selected creatures without removing any already summoned entities.
help.useless_stretcher.summon: Summon selected creatures in front of you, up to 32 types. Mob AI is disabled except necessary dragon logic. Requires server enablement; reports success.
help.useless_stretcher.recall: Remove your currently loaded summoned entities, leaving natural mobs alone. Dead or unloaded targets cannot be removed by this action.
help.useless_stretcher.fold: Expand/collapse extra controls such as summoning and loot refresh. Only changes visibility, not feature states.
help.useless_stretcher.fold_mod: Expand or collapse this mod group without changing selections.
help.useless_stretcher.select_entity: Select or deselect this creature, up to 32 types; press Summon when ready.
help.useless_stretcher.clear_patterns: Remove all fetched patterns and cancel pending fetches for this block. Mold selections are preserved.
help.useless_stretcher.all_molds: Toggle every mold in the loaded catalog at once. Click again to clear all mold selections; this does not fetch patterns.
help.useless_stretcher.mod_patterns: Fetch/remove this mod group's patterns for the filtered entries, without changing molds. Large recipe sets are processed incrementally.
help.useless_stretcher.mod_molds: Enable/disable the currently listed molds in this mod group. This does not fetch patterns.
help.useless_stretcher.fetch_pattern: Fetch/remove patterns for this machine. Shift-click applies the previous action across a range; Ctrl-click preserves the range anchor. Independent of molds.
help.useless_stretcher.enable_mold: Toggle this mold. Shift-click selects a range; Ctrl-click retains the range anchor. Small furnaces support single-mold recipes; use the multiblock hub for multiple molds.
help.useless_stretcher.server_config: Host changes synchronize to connected players after saving. Edit the category and press Save; dedicated servers use the corresponding server configuration file.
help.useless_stretcher.confirm_reclaim: Confirm stopping this acceleration and removing its record. Machines remain intact. Back cannot undo this action.
help.useless_stretcher.cancel_reclaim: Cancel reclaiming and return to the list, leaving acceleration unchanged.
help.useless_stretcher.increase: Increase this value by one step, up to its limit.
help.useless_stretcher.decrease: Decrease this value by one step, down to its limit.
help.useless_stretcher.previous: View the previous page without changing acceleration.
help.useless_stretcher.next: View the next page without changing acceleration.
gui.useless_stretcher.entity_acceleratio: Choose how entities accelerate. Original full ticks remain the default; timer mode is opt-in and never changes machines or ranges.
Original behavior: uses the main multiplier, up to x1024, to run complete entity ticks, including mod logic. Higher speeds cost more. Existing targets keep this mode.

Fast-forwards growth, breeding cooldowns and supported chicken, sheep, bee, turtle and villager timers/states, up to x32768. No extra full ticks, movement or unknown mod logic. Respects the server AI setting; multiplier is not output count. Shift-right-click the creature again to apply.
Biological timers x%s only; machines, AE and range speeds are unchanged. Uses the main 30-second/permanent setting. Reapply to the creature. Main multiplier Off still cancels acceleration.
Advances growth, breeding cooldowns and supported production timers, without extra full ticks. Uses the main duration mode. Reapply to targets after changing settings; main Off still cancels targets.
Uses the main multiplier (up to 1024) and complete entity ticks. Preserves existing behavior and costs more at high speeds. Timer multipliers only apply in timer mode.
